A Neighbourly Request Regarding the Shen Yun Poster in Your Window

​Dear [Business Name / Owner's Name],

​I am writing to you today as a neighbour, a regular patron, and a fellow community member. I have always appreciated how welcoming your business is and how you actively support local arts and events by sharing your storefront space. It shows a genuine commitment to enriching our neighbourhood, which is one of the many reasons I love stopping by.

​However, I am reaching out to share some well-documented and deeply concerning information regarding a poster currently displayed in your window: the advertisement for Shen Yun.

​While Shen Yun is heavily marketed as a beautiful, harmless celebration of traditional Chinese culture and dance, the reality behind the curtain is very different. The organization is operated and funded by Falun Dafa (also known as Falun Gong), a controversial religious movement. In recent years, major news outlets have uncovered overwhelming evidence of the physical and mental exploitation of the young artists who make the show possible.

​Here is what prominent investigative journalists and recent legal filings have brought to light:

1. ​The New York Times Investigation (2024): A major, multi-part exposé revealed that Shen Yun has generated hundreds of millions of dollars while relying heavily on the labour of teenagers and minors. Former dancers reported working gruelling, 15-hour days for little to no pay. The investigation highlighted a systemic culture of emotional abuse, noting that young performers were routinely discouraged from seeking professional medical treatment for serious injuries.
2. ​CBS News and Recent Lawsuits (2024–2026): Multiple class-action lawsuits have been filed by former dancers alleging extreme coercion and brutal working conditions. As covered by CBS and other outlets, former performers have testified to severe physical and mental control. This includes instructors dictating the dancers' eating habits and weight, forcing them to perform through severe injuries (including torn muscles), and using psychological tactics to keep them isolated at the group's compound in New York.
3. ​Canadian Institutional Backlash: Because of these disturbing, mounting allegations, major Canadian institutions are taking a stand. For example, the National Arts Centre (NAC) in Ottawa recently chose to sever ties and will no longer host Shen Yun, following internal reviews of the organization's conduct and treatment of vulnerable individuals.

​I know that by displaying this poster, your intention is simply to promote a colourful cultural event, not to endorse the exploitation of young artists. But as a community that values human rights, fair labour, and ethical treatment, it is important that we know who we are giving a platform to.

​I respectfully **urge you to remove the Shen Yun poster from your store**. By doing so, you are making a quiet but powerful choice not to provide free advertising to an organization accused of physically and mentally controlling its performers.

​Thank you so much for your time, your understanding, and your continued dedication to making our neighbourhood an ethical and wonderful place.

​Warmly,

​[Your Name]
[Your Contact Information / Neighbourhood Resident]
